newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan court rejects Okinawa rape case appeal.
newsitem.headline: Japan court rejects Okinawa rape case appeal.

text.p: A Japanese appeals court on Thursday rejected an appeal for shorter sentences by two U.S. servicemen convicted of raping an Okinawa schoolgirl last September, Japanese media reported.
The Naha branch of the Fukuoka High Court rejected the appeal by U.S. Marine Private Rodrico Harp, 22, and Marine Private Kendrick Ledet, 21.

In March, Harp and Ledet were sentenced to seven years and six-and-a-half years, respectively, for the abduction and rape of the 12-year-old Okinawan girl on September 4, 1995. Navy Seaman Marcus Gill, 23, who was sentenced to seven years, has not appealed.
The rape became a lightning rod for criticism by residents of U.S. military bases.

In a referendum on Sunday, Okinawans voted overwhelmingly to call for a reduction in the heavy U.S. military presence on the islands and prefectural governor Masahide Ota is pushing for a closure of all the bases by 2015.

The island, some 1,000 km (625 miles) southwest of Tokyo, is home to three-quarters of the U.S. military facilities in Japan. Following the rape, Ota staged a strong protest against the central government by refusing to sign land lease contracts for U.S. military facilities.
